books.section: Great Depression and the New Deal (1929-1939)

stimulus.text: Paraphrase of 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 23, and Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.10: When Roosevelt took office in March 1933, banks were failing as frightened depositors withdrew their money. He closed all banks for four days so the government could inspect them, and most reopened by March 15. The Banking Act of 1933 then created the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, which insured individual deposits. In the same first Hundred Days, Congress created the Civilian Conservation Corps, which gave young men work on forest and conservation projects; the Agricultural Adjustment Administration, which paid farmers to grow less so prices would rise; and the National Industrial Recovery Act, which set industry codes for wages, hours, and prices and displayed a Blue Eagle poster in shops that complied.

stem: According to the passage, why did the Agricultural Adjustment Administration pay farmers to grow less?

options.text: To feed hungry Americans with surplus crops
options.misconception: Paying farmers to grow less cut the food supply; the AAA raised prices by limiting output, not by feeding the hungry.
The AAA paid farmers rather than punishing them; the payments were meant to lift prices, not to penalize growers.

options.text: To move farmers into factory work
options.misconception: The AAA aimed to help farmers stay on the land by raising prices, not to move them into factories.

options.text: To raise farm prices by cutting overproduction

rationales.A: Background from the books: the AAA cut output while many went hungry, which is why the slaughter of pigs shocked people; feeding the hungry was not its method.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the AAA offered farmers payments, not punishment, in exchange for growing less so that prices would rise.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the AAA tried to make farming pay again, not to push farmers off the land into factory jobs.
rationales.D: Background from the books: farmers had overproduced while prices fell, so the AAA paid them to grow less and let scarcity lift prices.
rationales.general:
1. The passage says farmers were overproducing while prices fell.
2. The AAA answered by paying farmers to grow less.
3. Less supply meant higher prices for what farmers sold.
4. The goal was farm income, even though cutting output while people were hungry looked harsh.
Remember: when a policy pays people to produce less, ask which price it is trying to raise.
